A.explanation: Current of $10 \text{ A}$ loses $10 \text{ V}$ in the two $0.50 \text{ } \Omega$ wires, leaving $230 \text{ V}$ and $2.3 \text{ kW}$ for the kettle.

B.explanation: Power of $2.3 \text{ kW}$ is correct but $235 \text{ V}$ subtracts only one $5 \text{ V}$ wire drop instead of both wires.

C.explanation: P.d. of $230 \text{ V}$ is correct but power cannot stay $2.4 \text{ kW}$ because $100 \text{ W}$ is dissipated in the connecting wires.

D.explanation: Both values ignore the full loss, keeping $2.4 \text{ kW}$ and subtracting only $5 \text{ V}$ for one wire.

hints: Notice the supply gives $2.4 \text{ kW}$ at $240 \text{ V}$ - first find the circuit current from $P = VI$.
The same current flows through the kettle and both $0.50 \text{ } \Omega$ wires, so find the $IR$ drop in one wire and double it.
Subtract the total wire drop from $240 \text{ V}$ for the kettle p.d., then subtract the $I^2R$ wire loss from $2.4 \text{ kW}$ for the kettle power.
walkthrough: Find the current delivered by the supply using $P = VI$. $I = P/V = 2400/240 = 10 \text{ A}$.
This $10 \text{ A}$ flows in series through each $0.50 \text{ } \Omega$ connecting wire. Voltage drop in one wire is $V = IR = 10 \times 0.50 = 5.0 \text{ V}$.
Two wires give a total lost voltage of $2 \times 5.0 = 10 \text{ V}$. By Kirchhoff's loop rule the kettle p.d. is $240 - 10 = 230 \text{ V}$.
Power lost in the wires is $P = I^2R = 10^2 \times 1.0 = 100 \text{ W} = 0.10 \text{ kW}$, where $1.0 \text{ } \Omega$ is the total wire resistance.
Power to the kettle is supply power minus wire loss: $2.4 - 0.10 = 2.3 \text{ kW}$ with $230 \text{ V}$ across it. This is option A.
